# Token Mapping Guide

The single source of truth for which design tokens exist in this project,
their resolved values, and when to use each. Auto-generated from
`src/tokens/source/*.json` (DTCG) on every `pnpm tokens:build`.

## How tokens are exposed

Two consumption paths, both regenerated from the same source:

| Form | File | How to use |
|---|---|---|
| CSS custom properties | `src/styles/tokens.css` | `color: var(--theme-accent-default);` |
| TypeScript constants | `src/styles/tokens.ts` | `import { ThemeAccentDefault } from '…/tokens';` |
| Typography utility classes | `src/styles/typography.css` | `.heading { composes: text-styles-heading-1 from global; }` |

**Always reference semantic tokens over primitives.** `--primitives-palette-*`
are exposed for completeness but should not be consumed directly in component
code — use the `--theme-*`, `--spacing-*`, `--radius-*` aliases instead.

## Naming convention

Token names mirror the source path, kebab-cased and joined with `-`:

| Source path | CSS variable | TS export |
|---|---|---|
| `primitives.palette.sky.500` | `--primitives-palette-sky-500` | `PrimitivesPaletteSky500` |
| `theme.accent.default` | `--theme-accent-default` | `ThemeAccentDefault` |
| `spacing.4` | `--spacing-4` | `Spacing4` |
| `effectStyles.blur.tailwind.layer.md` | `--effect-styles-blur-tailwind-layer-md` | `EffectStylesBlurTailwindLayerMd` |

## Notes on special token shapes

- **Shadow tokens** (`$type: "shadow"`) are emitted as ready-to-use
  `box-shadow` strings in CSS, and as arrays of layer objects in TS.
- **Blur tokens** (`effectStyles.blur.*`) carry a `{ kind, radius }` shape;
  the CSS variable holds only the radius, so consumers compose
  `filter: blur(var(--effect-styles-blur-tailwind-layer-md))` for layer
  blurs and `backdrop-filter: blur(var(--effect-styles-blur-backdrop))`
  for backdrop blurs. The `kind` is preserved in the token's description.
- **Reference tokens** stay as `var(--…)` chains in CSS so theme overrides
  cascade naturally; the TS export resolves to the final literal value.

## effectStyles

_Effect Styles — shadows, focus rings, blur radii._

### effectStyles.shadow

- `--effect-styles-shadow-surface` / `EffectStylesShadowSurface` — `0px 0px 1px 0px #0000000F, 0px 1px 2px 0px #0000000F, 0px 2px 4px 0px #0000000A` — Generic surface elevation.
- `--effect-styles-shadow-field` / `EffectStylesShadowField` — `0px 0px 1px 0px #0000000F, 0px 1px 2px 0px #0000000F, 0px 2px 4px 0px #0000000A, inset 0px 0px 0px 0px #FFFFFF1A` — Default field elevation (with inner highlight).
- `--effect-styles-shadow-switch` / `EffectStylesShadowSwitch` — `0px 0px 5px 0px #00000005, 0px 2px 10px 0px #0000000F, 0px 0px 1px 0px #0000004D` — Switch / toggle elevation.
- `--effect-styles-shadow-tab` / `EffectStylesShadowTab` — `0px 2px 8px 0px #0000000F` — Tab indicator elevation.
- `--effect-styles-shadow-overlay` / `EffectStylesShadowOverlay` — `0px 14px 28px 0px #00000014, 0px -6px 12px 0px #00000008, 0px 2px 8px 0px #0000000F` — Modal / popover elevation. Pair with effectStyles.blur.backdrop.
- `--effect-styles-shadow-inner` / `EffectStylesShadowInner` — `inset 0px 0px 1px 0px #0000004D` — Inset shadow.
- `--effect-styles-shadow-tailwind-sm` / `EffectStylesShadowTailwindSm` — `0px 1px 2px 0px #0000000D`
- `--effect-styles-shadow-tailwind-default` / `EffectStylesShadowTailwindDEFAULT` — `0px 1px 3px 0px #0000001A, 0px 1px 2px -1px #0000001A`
- `--effect-styles-shadow-tailwind-md` / `EffectStylesShadowTailwindMd` — `0px 4px 6px -1px #0000001A, 0px 2px 4px -2px #0000001A`
- `--effect-styles-shadow-tailwind-lg` / `EffectStylesShadowTailwindLg` — `0px 10px 15px -3px #0000001A, 0px 4px 6px -4px #0000001A`
- `--effect-styles-shadow-tailwind-xl` / `EffectStylesShadowTailwindXl` — `0px 20px 25px -5px #0000001A, 0px 8px 10px -6px #0000001A`
- `--effect-styles-shadow-tailwind-2xl` / `EffectStylesShadowTailwind2xl` — `0px 25px 50px -12px #00000040`
- `--effect-styles-shadow-tailwind-inner` / `EffectStylesShadowTailwindInner` — `inset 0px 2px 4px 0px #0000000D`

### effectStyles.focus

- `--effect-styles-focus-ring` / `EffectStylesFocusRing` — `0px 0px 0px 4px #0EA5E9, 0px 0px 0px 2px #F5F5F5` — Represent a focus state. Standard focus ring (accent + 2px white offset).
- `--effect-styles-focus-ring-field` / `EffectStylesFocusRingField` — `0px 0px 0px 2px #0EA5E9` — Represent a focus state. Compact focus ring for field inputs.

### effectStyles.blur

- `--effect-styles-blur-default` / `EffectStylesBlurDefault` — `0px` — .blur-default – Use it for translucent overlays (without a blur).
- `--effect-styles-blur-backdrop` / `EffectStylesBlurBackdrop` — `12px` — .blur-backdrop – Use it for blurred overlays.
- `--effect-styles-blur-tailwind-layer-none` / `EffectStylesBlurTailwindLayerNone` — `0px`
- `--effect-styles-blur-tailwind-layer-sm` / `EffectStylesBlurTailwindLayerSm` — `4px`
- `--effect-styles-blur-tailwind-layer-default` / `EffectStylesBlurTailwindLayerDEFAULT` — `8px`
- `--effect-styles-blur-tailwind-layer-md` / `EffectStylesBlurTailwindLayerMd` — `12px`

## textStyles

_Typography composites — apply via `composes: <class> from global;`_

- `.text-styles-heading-1` — Used for the main screen title, should be used only once per screen. It pairs with base body.
- `.text-styles-heading-2` — Used for main section titles within a screen. Provides hierarchy below Heading 1 and should be used sparingly. Pairs with body base.
- `.text-styles-heading-3` — Used for subsection titles or important content blocks. Helps break down information within a section. Pairs with body sm or body base.
- `.text-styles-heading-4` — Used for subsection titles or important content blocks. Helps break down information within a section. Pairs with body sm or body base.
- `.text-styles-body-base` — Default paragraph style for most content. Optimized for readability at medium sizes.
- `.text-styles-body-base-medium` — Same as body base, but with medium font weight. Provides subtle emphasis for key points, labels, or short content blocks.
- `.text-styles-body-sm` — Used for secondary or supporting text. Ideal for captions, metadata, and content with lower emphasis.
- `.text-styles-body-sm-medium` — Same as body small, but with medium font weight. Provides stronger emphasis for small text.
- `.text-styles-body-xs` — Used for fine print, footnotes, and dense UI elements where space is limited.
- `.text-styles-body-xs-medium` — Same as body xs, but with medium font weight. Adds clarity and hierarchy in tight spaces.
- `.text-styles-link-base` — Default link style for inline navigation or actions.
- `.text-styles-link-sm` — Used for inline links in smaller text contexts.
- `.text-styles-link-sm-hover` — Hover state for inline small links.
- `.text-styles-text-field-base` — Used for input text in standard fields. Optimized for readability at medium size.
- `.text-styles-text-field-sm` — Used for input text in compact fields.
- `.text-styles-button-base` — Primary button text style.
- `.text-styles-button-sm` — Button text style for compact buttons.

## Tips

1. **Never hardcode values.** Always reference a CSS variable or TS export.
2. **Prefer semantic over primitive.** `--theme-*` / `--spacing-*` /
   `--radius-*` are the consumption surface; `--primitives-*` are inputs.
3. **Check for state variants.** Most theme tokens have `-default`, `-hover`,
   and sometimes `-soft` / `-soft-hover` / `-foreground` companions.
4. **Typography tokens are composite.** Apply via
   `composes: text-styles-<name> from global;` — don't try to recreate them
   with individual font-* declarations.
5. **Light / dark modes.** Tokens whose source carries
   `$extensions.modes` switch values per active theme. The default emission
   is the light value.
